root_cause.text: bpf_iter_unix_seq_show() used lock_sock_fast() to hold an AF_UNIX socket’s slock while running a BPF iterator program, allowing that program’s sockmap update path to re-acquire the same socket lock via bh_lock_sock() and deadlock recursively.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces lock_sock_fast()/unlock_sock_fast() with lock_sock()/release_sock() in bpf_iter_unix_seq_show(), and the commit/CVE explicitly show the deadlock occurring because __lock_sock_fast already held slock-AF_UNIX when sock_map_update_elem() tried to take the same lock through bh_lock_sock().

intent_record.intent_summary: Use normal socket locking and check for dead sockets instead of unhashed ones to avoid iterating over invalid UNIX sockets and incorrectly skipping valid ones.
intent_record.what: The code removes the local boolean variable `slow`, replaces `slow = lock_sock_fast(sk);` with `lock_sock(sk);`, and changes the subsequent socket state check from `sk_unhashed(sk)` to `sock_flag(sk, SOCK_DEAD)` before jumping to the unlock path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now always takes the regular socket lock path instead of the fast-lock variant and skips processing when the socket is marked dead rather than merely unhashed, preventing iteration logic from operating on sockets that have been destroyed while avoiding incorrectly skipping sockets based only on unhashed state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use release_sock() instead of unlock_sock_fast() in bpf_iter_unix_seq_show() to correctly release the socket lock via the standard unlock path.
intent_record.what: The code replaces the socket unlock call in bpf_iter_unix_seq_show() from unlock_sock_fast(sk, slow) to release_sock(sk), and removes the use of the slow argument at that call site.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now always releases the socket using the standard release_sock() path instead of the fast unlock helper, changing the locking teardown behavior to use the normal socket release mechanism and avoiding dependence on the slow-mode state for unlocking.
